author_reading_scope: All four complete PDFs were fetched and inspected. The exact relevant sections are listed per source; this records inspection of those full sections, not sequential reading of unrelated pages.

sources.title: Bernardo Cockburn, An Introduction to the Discontinuous Galerkin Method for Convection-Dominated Problems, complete CIME lecture notes

author_read_locators.locator: §§3.2–3.6 and §3.16, printed pp. 161–169 and 189–200: broken polynomial spaces, the elementwise weak form, numerical fluxes, L2 projection, linear stability, and the complete projection-based error proof; §4.2, printed pp. 201–203: multidimensional DG weak form and quadrature.

harvest.name: §§3.2–3.4: broken polynomial trial space, elementwise weak DG form, and consistent upwind numerical flux
harvest.detail: The local definition states the one-dimensional and affine-simplicial branches, exact trace directions, and boundary data; its full flux convention is scaffolded as the DG item.

harvest.name: §3.5: L2 projection onto the local polynomial space and diagonal mass matrix
harvest.detail: The projection equations are defined locally, and the finite-dimensional existence, orthogonality, and best-approximation proof is supplied in the local lemma.

harvest.name: §§3.6 and 3.16: linear DG L2 stability and projection-based error estimates with complete proof appendix
harvest.detail: The cited proof route motivates projection, consistency, and upwind dissipation. The submitted theorem proves its own exact trace-residual estimate and does not import the source's separate asymptotic-order statements.

harvest.name: §4.2: multidimensional element weak form, numerical face flux, and quadrature assumptions
harvest.detail: The multidimensional DG definition states the matching affine mesh, outward normal, paired trace, and face-flux convention used in this source section.

harvest.name: §§3.8–3.10: SSP/TVD Runge–Kutta transfer requires stability of each forward-Euler map
harvest.detail: Only the conditional transfer principle is context. The local theorem uses the exact published SSPRK(3,3) supplier and proves the particular degree-zero upwind forward-Euler bound before applying it.

harvest.name: §§3.7 and 3.12–3.13: nonlinear RKDG limiter and TVDM/T VBM arguments
harvest.detail: The source discusses limiter-based stability and variation arguments, while the assigned nonlinear claim is a distinct SBP flux-differencing entropy proof; no limiter theorem is needed for that proof.
harvest.reason: These limiter-based scalar stability arguments do not prove the assigned Tadmor flux-differencing entropy inequality; that distinct SBP claim is proved locally from the exact matrix and paired-face identities.

harvest.name: §§3.2–3.4: one-dimensional interval partition, cells, and left/right traces
harvest.detail: The local definition fixes the ordered interval partition, orientation, endpoint normals, and jump convention for the one-dimensional branch.

harvest.name: §3.6: semidiscrete L2 stability for linear transport
harvest.detail: The source treats the one-dimensional upwind energy calculation; the local theorem supplies and proves the affine-simplex multidimensional face-pairing extension.

harvest.name: §3.16: projection orthogonality in the linear error argument
harvest.detail: The source uses the unique L2 projection in its error identity; the local lemma separately proves existence, uniqueness, and best approximation from the full-support hypothesis.

harvest.name: §§3.2–3.5: degree-zero upwind update as a shared-flux cell balance
harvest.detail: The source supplies the piecewise-constant DG and shared-flux context; the local algorithm gives the exact multidimensional cell-volume and face-area update.

sources.title: Bernardo Cockburn and Chi-Wang Shu, Runge–Kutta Discontinuous Galerkin Methods for Convection-Dominated Problems, Journal of Scientific Computing 16 (2001)

author_read_locators.locator: §1.1 and §§2.1–2.5, printed pp. 175–195: DG weak formulation, monotone/upwind fluxes, SSP convex-combination recursion, and the forward-Euler stability condition; §3.1, printed pp. 201–203: multidimensional DG space discretization.

harvest.name: §1.1: DG space discretization, explicit Runge–Kutta stages, and conditional stability transfer
harvest.detail: The review supplies the general SSP design context. The exact three-stage coefficients and the only admitted forward-Euler entropy claim are stated and proved from the authored and published local interfaces.

harvest.name: §2.1: weak DG form, L2 initial projection, and monotone numerical flux assumptions
harvest.detail: The local DG definition adopts the weak element form and states its own scalar transport flux and boundary-trace hypotheses.

harvest.name: §§2.2–2.3: SSP convex combinations and forward-Euler step restrictions
harvest.detail: The review explicitly requires a stable forward-Euler map before transferring a convex bound. The local CFL proof supplies that map for degree-zero upwind DG; no high-order forward-Euler stability is inferred.

harvest.name: §2.3: forward Euler is not generally L2-stable for degree at least one DG spaces
harvest.detail: This limitation is retained: the SSP result is confined to the proved degree-zero spatial operator and is not transferred to the high-order DG or nonlinear SBP method.

harvest.name: §3.1: multidimensional DG weak form and local face fluxes
harvest.detail: The assigned DG definition includes this multidimensional face-flux setting and gives its matching affine mesh and orientation conventions.

sources.title: Travis C. Fisher and Mark H. Carpenter, High-Order Entropy Stable Finite Difference Schemes for Nonlinear Conservation Laws: Finite Domains, NASA/TM-2013-217971

author_read_locators.locator: §2.3.2, printed p. 8; §§3.1–3.2, printed pp. 13–20; §4.2.3, printed pp. 31–35: diagonal-norm SBP identity, entropy-conservative two-point fluxes, entropy-stable flux differencing, and semidiscrete entropy analysis.

harvest.name: §2.3.2: positive diagonal norm and Q-transpose identity for SBP differentiation
harvest.detail: The local definition states the multidirectional face-restriction form of the exact SBP identity and separately requires constant preservation and paired face quadrature.

harvest.name: §§3.1–3.2: semidiscrete entropy contraction and the Tadmor two-point jump condition
harvest.detail: The local method definition gives the directional Tadmor identity and exact SBP volume/face data; the following local theorem proves the paired-face balance.

harvest.name: §4.2.3: entropy-stable spatial discretization from SBP and face flux conditions
harvest.detail: The local theorem proves conservation and the exact entropy balance for the stated affine-element paired-node method, including its explicit entropy-variable jump dissipation.

harvest.name: §2.5: a non-SSP time integrator does not inherit the formal semidiscrete proof
harvest.detail: The caution is preserved: no fully discrete entropy claim follows from the high-order semidiscrete theorem.

sources.title: Eitan Tadmor, Entropy Stable Schemes, Handbook of Numerical Methods for Hyperbolic Problems, Vol. 17 (2016)

author_read_locators.locator: §§4.1–4.3 and §5.1, printed pp. 477–480 and 484–485: entropy variables and potentials, the entropy-conservative jump identity, positive-semidefinite numerical viscosity, and the additional forward-time entropy-production term.

harvest.name: §4.1: entropy variables and the entropy potential
harvest.detail: The local method defines the directional entropy variables and potentials, using the exact PE03 entropy-pair convention.

harvest.name: §4.2: entropy-conservative two-point flux and entropy-stable dissipation
harvest.detail: The local method uses symmetric directional entropy-conservative fluxes and explicitly adds a nonnegative multiple of the entropy-variable jump at each interior node.

harvest.name: §4.3: semidiscrete entropy stability by comparing numerical and entropy-conservative viscosity
harvest.detail: The local theorem proves the semidiscrete entropy balance from the exact SBP identities and the prescribed interface flux.

harvest.name: §5.1: fully discrete entropy requires spatial viscosity to dominate the additional time-differencing entropy production
harvest.detail: This confirms that semidiscrete entropy stability alone is insufficient. The SSP theorem is restricted to the separate degree-zero forward-Euler bound actually proved here.
